A.explanation: Upward force is $30 + 50 = 80 \text{ N}$ but downward force is $90 \text{ N}$, so resultant force is not zero even though moments $30 \times 50$ and $50 \times 30$ balance.

B.explanation: Resultant force is zero because $36 + 70 = 106 \text{ N}$ upward balances $106 \text{ N}$ downward, but moments $36 \times 50 = 1800 \text{ N cm}$ and $70 \times 30 = 2100 \text{ N cm}$ do not balance.

C.explanation: Resultant force is zero because $28 + 35 = 63 \text{ N}$ upward balances $63 \text{ N}$ downward, but moments $28 \times 50 = 1400 \text{ N cm}$ and $35 \times 30 = 1050 \text{ N cm}$ do not balance.

D.explanation: Upward force $42 + 70 = 112 \text{ N}$ balances $112 \text{ N}$ downward, and moments $42 \times 50 = 2100 \text{ N cm}$ and $70 \times 30 = 2100 \text{ N cm}$ are equal and opposite.

hints: First add the two upward forces on each beam and compare with the single downward force - only beams with zero vector sum can be in translational equilibrium.
Then take moments about the downward $90 \text{ N}$ to $112 \text{ N}$ force, so only the $50 \text{ cm}$ left force and $30 \text{ cm}$ right force contribute.
Check if left moment equals right moment: compare $(\text{left force} \times 50 \text{ cm})$ with $(\text{right force} \times 30 \text{ cm})$ for opposite clockwise and anticlockwise torques.
walkthrough: Take upward as positive. For equilibrium the resultant force must be zero, so sum of the two upward forces must equal the downward force.
Beam A gives $30 + 50 - 90 = -10 \text{ N}$, so it fails. Beams B, C and D give $36 + 70 - 106 = 0$, $28 + 35 - 63 = 0$ and $42 + 70 - 112 = 0$, so all three have zero resultant force.
For zero resultant torque, take moments about the central downward force. The downward force has zero moment arm, so its moment is zero.

The left upward force $50 \text{ cm}$ away and the right upward force $30 \text{ cm}$ away produce opposite torques. Their magnitudes are $F_{left} \times 50 \text{ cm}$ and $F_{right} \times 30 \text{ cm}$.

Calculate: B gives $1800 \text{ N cm}$ against $2100 \text{ N cm}$, C gives $1400 \text{ N cm}$ against $1050 \text{ N cm}$, D gives $42 \times 50 = 2100 \text{ N cm}$ against $70 \times 30 = 2100 \text{ N cm}$.
Only D has both zero resultant force and balanced opposite moments, so zero resultant torque. This is option D.
